title: Magnetic-Field-Driven Dimensional Reduction in a Quantum Antiferromagnet
authors: Subhankar Khatua, Marcin Raczkowski, Jeroen van den Brink, Fakher F. Assaad
abstract: Low dimensionality enhances quantum fluctuations, triggering novel states of quantum matter to emerge. In real materials, low dimensionality usually arises from spatially strongly anisotropic couplings. Here, we demonstrate a different mechanism: in two-dimensional systems with coupled alternating ferromagnetic (FM) and antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin-$1/2$ chains, an applied magnetic field may drive a dimensional reduction. Under magnetic field, the FM chains polarize and stiffen, suppressing the propagation of transverse AFM fluctuations from one chain to another, and effectively induce one-dimensional behavior at low energies. For a model describing botallackite, Cu$_2$(OH)$_3$Br, quantum Monte Carlo dynamics show that beyond a critical magnetic field, the low-energy spectrum reduces to that of a one-dimensional AFM Heisenberg spin-$1/2$ chain with field-dependent incommensurate two-spinon fluctuations, providing clear signatures for inelastic neutron scattering.
summary: The paper demonstrates that applying a strong magnetic field can drive dimensional reduction in a 2D quantum antiferromagnet model. By analyzing the system's spin dynamics via QMC simulations, the authors show that interchain correlations are suppressed, causing the low-energy spectrum to map onto that of an isolated 1D Heisenberg chain.
main_problem: The study investigates whether an external magnetic field can induce a dimensional reduction in a quasi-two-dimensional quantum antiferromagnet.
main_result: Beyond a critical magnetic field, the system's low-energy excitations are predicted to reduce to those of a one-dimensional AFM Heisenberg chain, exhibiting gapless incommensurate spinon fluctuations.
method: The research employs Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations using Abrikosov fermions and compares results with analytical treatments like spin-wave theory and Bethe Ansatz analysis for limits.
model_or_system: The model is a quasi-2D quantum magnet based on the mineral botallackite, featuring alternating ferromagnetic (FM) and antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin-1/2 Heisenberg chains coupled together. The Hamiltonian includes interchain couplings that are tuned by an external magnetic field.
key_observables: Total magnetization ($M$), dynamical structure factor ($S(\mathbf{Q}, \omega)$), static structure factor, and the evolution of spectral weight in these quantities as a function of $B$ and $T$.
important_parameters: The critical magnetic field ($B_c \approx 16	ext{ T}$), temperature ($T$), and the relative strengths of intra-chain vs. inter-chain couplings ($J_2 > J_1 > J_3$).
main_assumptions: The model simplifies by omitting easy-axis anisotropy and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, focusing on SU(2)-symmetric exchange terms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the magnetization curve vs. field (Fig. 1b), and show how the dynamical structure factor evolves from a 2D pattern to one characteristic of decoupled 1D chains at high fields (Figs. 2, 3, 4).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the model and calculating magnetization curves; it then analyzes the spectral weight evolution using QMC simulations across varying magnetic fields, demonstrating the crossover to 1D behavior.
why_interesting: This work provides a clear example of tuning dimensionality in quantum magnets using external fields, offering measurable spectroscopic signatures (inelastic neutron scattering) for emergent low-dimensional physics.
